- conda-forge

about.description:
pgAdmin 4 is a web-based administration and development platform for
PostgreSQL. It provides a graphical interface for browsing and editing
database objects, a query tool with syntax highlighting and explain plan
visualisation, a debugger for PL/pgSQL, backup and restore front-ends for
the standard PostgreSQL utilities, and dashboards for server and session
activity.

This package installs the server (web) mode of pgAdmin 4. Start it with the
`pgadmin4` command and connect a browser to the address it prints; use
`pgadmin4-cli` for the setup and user-management commands. The client-side
assets are prebuilt and shipped in the upstream wheel.
about.license: PostgreSQL AND MIT AND ISC AND BSD-2-Clause AND BSD-3-Clause AND (Apache-2.0 OR MPL-2.0) AND Apache-2.0 AND OFL-1.1 AND CC-BY-4.0
about.license_family: PostgreSQL AND MIT AND ISC AND BSD-2-Clause AND BSD-3-Clause AND (Apache-2.0 OR MPL-2.0) AND Apache-2.0 AND OFL-1.1 AND CC-BY-4.0
about.summary: pgAdmin 4 -- the open source management and development platform for PostgreSQL

script: ${{ PYTHON }} -c "import zipfile; z = zipfile.ZipFile('pgadmin4-${{ version }}-py3-none-any.whl'); z.extract('pgadmin4/LICENSE'); z.extractall(members=[n for n in z.namelist() if n.endswith('.js.LICENSE.txt')])"
${{ PYTHON }} -c "import os, sysconfig; [os.path.exists(p) and os.remove(p) for p in (os.path.join(sysconfig.get_path('scripts'), n) for n in ('pgadmin4', 'pgadmin4-cli'))]"

raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  version: "9.17"

package:
  name: pgadmin4
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  # pgAdmin 4 has never published an sdist on PyPI -- only a py3-none-any wheel.
  # rattler-build does not unpack ".whl" files, so the wheel is copied into
  # $SRC_DIR verbatim and installed directly by the build script below.
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/py3/p/pgadmin4/pgadmin4-${{ version }}-py3-none-any.whl
  sha256: f11d217e6fcfea8573c297d8228082a921c6a553020cc130d0fcda3ae87e4684

build:
  noarch: python
  number: 0
  script:
    # Pull pgAdmin's own licence plus the webpack-emitted third-party notices for
    # the prebuilt JS bundles out of the wheel, so `about.license_file` finds them.
    - ${{ PYTHON }} -c "import zipfile; z = zipfile.ZipFile('pgadmin4-${{ version }}-py3-none-any.whl'); z.extract('pgadmin4/LICENSE'); z.extractall(members=[n for n in z.namelist() if n.endswith('.js.LICENSE.txt')])"
    - ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install pgadmin4-${{ version }}-py3-none-any.whl --no-deps --no-build-isolation -vv
    # Install the conda-specific console-script wrapper next to the upstream
    # modules, so it is importable as pgadmin4.conda_entry.
    - ${{ PYTHON }} -c "import os, shutil, sysconfig; shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(os.environ['RECIPE_DIR'], 'conda_entry.py'), os.path.join(sysconfig.get_path('purelib'), 'pgadmin4', 'conda_entry.py'))"
    # Drop the POSIX launchers pip generated -- they are useless on Windows for a
    # noarch package. rattler-build regenerates both from build.python.entry_points.
    - ${{ PYTHON }} -c "import os, sysconfig; [os.path.exists(p) and os.remove(p) for p in (os.path.join(sysconfig.get_path('scripts'), n) for n in ('pgadmin4', 'pgadmin4-cli'))]"

  python:
    entry_points:
      # Both scripts go through conda_entry rather than upstream's
      # pgAdmin4:main / setup:main -- see conda_entry.py for why.
      - pgadmin4 = pgadmin4.conda_entry:main
      - pgadmin4-cli = pgadmin4.conda_entry:cli_main

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - pip
    # Not actually invoked -- a prebuilt wheel is installed with
    # --no-build-isolation -- but conda-forge's linter requires a build backend
    # to be declared whenever `pip` appears in host. setuptools built the wheel.
    - setuptools
  run:
    - python >=${{ python_min }}
    # Upstream pins every dependency with "==". Those pins are relaxed here to
    # ranges that keep the intended API compatibility while remaining solvable
    # against the rest of conda-forge.
    - authlib >=1.7,<1.8
    - azure-identity >=1.25.3,<2
    - azure-mgmt-rdbms >=10.1.1,<11
    # <26 is not cosmetic: 26.0.0 dropped the aggregate azure.mgmt.resource
    # namespace, so pgadmin.misc.cloud.azure's
    # `from azure.mgmt.resource import ResourceManagementClient` fails.
    - azure-mgmt-resource >=25.0.0,<26
    - azure-mgmt-subscription >=3.1.1,<4
    - bcrypt >=5.0,<6
    - boto3 >=1.43,<2
    - certifi >=2026.6.17
    - cryptography >=49.0
    - flask >=3.1,<4
    - flask-babel >=4.0,<5
    - flask-compress >=1,<2
    - flask-login >=0.6,<1
    - flask-mail >=0.9,<1
    - flask-migrate >=4,<5
    - flask-paranoid >=0.3,<1
    - flask-security-too >=5.8,<6
    - flask-socketio >=5.6,<6
    - flask-sqlalchemy >=3.1,<4
    - flask-wtf >=1.3,<2
    - google-api-python-client >=2,<3
    - google-auth-oauthlib >=1.4.0,<2
    - jsonformatter >=0.3.4,<0.4
    - keyring >=25,<26
    - ldap3 >=2,<3
    - libgravatar >=1.0,<2
    - paramiko >=3.5.1
    - passlib >=1,<2
    - psutil >=7.2,<8
    - psycopg >=3.3.4,<4
    - pyotp >=2,<3
    - python-dateutil >=2,<3
    - pytz
    - qrcode >=8,<9
    - pillow  # the "pil" extra of qrcode
    - setuptools
    - sqlalchemy >=2,<3
    - sqlparse >=0.4,<1
    - sshtunnel >=0.4,<1
    - typer >=0.26,<1
    - urllib3 >=2.7,<3
    - user-agents >=2.2.0,<3
    - werkzeug >=3.1,<4
    - wtforms >=3.2,<4
    - if: linux
      then: __linux
    - if: osx
      then: __osx
    - if: win
      then:
        - __win
        - pywinpty >=2,<3

tests:
  - python:
      # Only the top-level package: pgadmin4.pgAdmin4 builds the Flask app at
      # import time and, in server mode, writes to /var/lib/pgadmin, so a bare
      # `python -c "import pgadmin4.pgAdmin4"` fails with EACCES. The script
      # test below covers that module through conda_entry, which is how the
      # console scripts reach it.
      imports:
        - pgadmin4
      # A noarch package installs on every Python at or above python_min, so
      # exercise both ends of that range.
      python_version:
        - ${{ python_min }}.*
        - "*"
      # pip_check is disabled: upstream's metadata pins every dependency with
      # "==", so `pip check` always fails against the relaxed conda-forge pins.
      pip_check: false
  # Importing pgadmin4.pgAdmin4 builds the Flask app at module scope, so it
  # needs a writable DATA_DIR; the helper script redirects it before importing.
  - script:
      - python test_import.py
    requirements:
      run:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    files:
      recipe:
        - test_import.py
  # The `pgadmin4-cli` script routes through conda_entry, so running it both
  # proves the wrapper resolves and that it creates its data directories.
  - script:
      - pgadmin4-cli --help
    requirements:
      run:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
  - package_contents:
      site_packages:
        - pgadmin4/conda_entry.py
        - pgadmin4/pgAdmin4.py
        - pgadmin4/pgadmin/__init__.py
        # The prebuilt web assets are the reason this recipe uses the wheel.
        - pgadmin4/pgadmin/static/js/generated/app.bundle.js

about:
  homepage: https://www.pgadmin.org/
  summary: pgAdmin 4 -- the open source management and development platform for PostgreSQL
  description: |
    pgAdmin 4 is a web-based administration and development platform for
    PostgreSQL. It provides a graphical interface for browsing and editing
    database objects, a query tool with syntax highlighting and explain plan
    visualisation, a debugger for PL/pgSQL, backup and restore front-ends for
    the standard PostgreSQL utilities, and dashboards for server and session
    activity.

    This package installs the server (web) mode of pgAdmin 4. Start it with the
    `pgadmin4` command and connect a browser to the address it prints; use
    `pgadmin4-cli` for the setup and user-management commands. The client-side
    assets are prebuilt and shipped in the upstream wheel.
  # pgAdmin's own code is under the PostgreSQL licence. The wheel also ships
  # prebuilt JS bundles that vendor third-party code; every bundled component's
  # notice is permissive (MIT/ISC/BSD-3-Clause, DOMPurify dual Apache-2.0 or
  # MPL-2.0, Font Awesome icons CC-BY-4.0 and fonts OFL-1.1). No copyleft.
  license: PostgreSQL AND MIT AND ISC AND BSD-2-Clause AND BSD-3-Clause AND (Apache-2.0 OR MPL-2.0) AND Apache-2.0 AND OFL-1.1 AND CC-BY-4.0
  license_file:
    - pgadmin4/LICENSE
    - pgadmin4/pgadmin/static/js/generated/*.js.LICENSE.txt
    # The webpack-emitted *.js.LICENSE.txt files above are attribution notices
    # naming each bundled component's licence; they do not carry the full
    # terms. licenses/ holds the complete SPDX texts they refer to.
    - licenses/
  documentation: https://www.pgadmin.org/docs/
  repository: https://github.com/pgadmin-org/pgadmin4

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - millsks
